questions.q: Why can't real-time data quality checks wait for a nightly batch job the way Databricks & Delta Lake's Lesson 36 medallion checks can?
options: Streaming systems never actually have data quality problems
There's no real difference in urgency between the two
Batch quality checks are always more accurate than streaming ones
A bad value streaming into a live dashboard is visible to someone right now, not discovered in tomorrow's quality report
questions.explain: The blast radius of a bad value is measured in seconds for a live system, not overnight.

questions.q: What does a range check catch that a null check doesn't?
options: Missing required fields entirely
Duplicate events arriving twice
A source that stopped sending a field it used to send
Values that are technically present but nonsensical, like a negative fare
questions.explain: Null checks catch missing fields; range checks catch present values that are still wrong.

questions.q: What does a schema drift check catch?
options: A fare amount that's negative
An event arriving out of order
A source that started sending a field it never sent before, or stopped sending one it used to — often an unannounced upstream change
A trip with a missing TripId
questions.explain: This is a distinct problem from missing or out-of-range values — it's about the shape of the data changing unexpectedly.

questions.q: Which existing tools from this chapter can be reused to catch bad events in-stream, without needing a new tool?
options: The Filter node (Lesson 35) to catch events before they land, and routing (Lesson 36) to send failures to a dedicated destination
Only Power BI's Direct Lake mode
Only the Fabric Warehouse's T-SQL engine
Only a brand-new Fabric item designed specifically for data quality
questions.explain: Activator (Lesson 37) can also alert on an unusual failure rate, rather than waiting for a human to notice.

questions.q: Why does a streaming data quality bug carry a higher real-world stake than the same bug in a nightly batch job, despite having a shorter time window?
options: Streaming systems don't feed any decisions that matter
Streaming bugs are always less severe than batch bugs
There's no meaningful difference in real-world impact between the two
It puts wrong numbers in front of a dispatcher, rider-facing map, or automated alerting rule making real-time decisions, rather than just delaying a report
questions.explain: A delayed report is a nuisance; a wrong number driving a live decision is a more immediate, visible failure.
